rows.label: Concept
rows.text: Trigonometric identities are the working grammar: true for **every** admissible angle, proved by transformation, never solved. Everything descends from the **unit circle**: sin²θ + cos²θ = 1, and by division 1 + tan²θ = sec²θ, 1 + cot²θ = cosec²θ.…

rows.label: Conditions
rows.text: x sin(A+B) = sin A + sin B. x Must use compound angle formula.  ·  x tan 2A = 2 tan A. x tan 2A = 2tan A/(1-tan^2 A).

rows.label: Special cases
rows.text: sec 90° = 1/cos 90° and tan 90° = sin 90°/cos 90° are undefined because cos 90° = 0, and cosec 0° is undefined because sin 0° = 0.  ·  The double angle formulas are just the compound angle formulas with B = A, so a proof of one family gives the other.

rows.label: Solved
rows.text: ***The telescoping trick*** — multiply cos th + cos 3th + ... + cos(2n-1)th by 2 sin th: each product becomes a difference of sines and the middle terms cancel, leaving sin 2nth (NEB 2020's proof in one move).

rows.label: Limitation
rows.text: Verified PYQs: NEB 2021 (standard values evaluation), NEB 2020 (cosine series proof) — assigned to this row. Other items are NEB-style practice.

rows.label: Derivation
rows.text: Given one trigonometric ratio and the quadrant of the angle, find all the other ratios by applying the relevant identity and the signs of that quadrant.  ·  Prove an identity by starting from one side and transforming it, line by line, into the other side using the fundamental identities.

rows.label: Shortcut
rows.text: Prove identities: start from the complicated side, convert to sines and cosines, hunt sin^2 + cos^2 = 1. cos(A-B) keeps a PLUS sign. tan(A+B) has minus in the denominator. r-formula: r = sqrt(a^2+b^2), max = r, min = -r.

rows.label: Quick concepts
rows.text: An identity is used, not solved: the proof walks one side into the other with known identities — no value of theta is ever substituted.

rows.label: Key points
rows.text: Fundamental identity: sin^2 th + cos^2 th = 1; dividing gives 1 + tan^2 th = sec^2 th and 1 + cot^2 th = cosec^2 th. Addition formulas: sin(A+B) = sinA cosB + cosA sinB; cos(A-B) = cosA cosB + sinA sinB; tan(A+B) = (tanA+tanB)/(1 - tanA tanB).…

rows.label: Universal facts
rows.text: Every identity in the syllabus descends from one geometric fact: the unit circle point (cos th, sin th) lies at distance 1 from the origin.

rows.label: Study notes
rows.text: ## 1. Topic Introduction — Identities Are the Grammar of Trigonometry A trigonometric **identity** is an equation true for **every** admissible angle — not solved, but *used*. The syllabus theorem set: the **fundamental identity** sin²θ + cos²θ = 1, the **addition formulas**, the **double/half-angle formulas**, the **transformation formulas** (sum ↔ product), and the…  ·  ## 2. Fundamental Concepts ### 2.1 The fundamental identity and its family - **Theorem (Pythagorean identity):** for every angle θ, **sin²θ + cos²θ = 1**. - Proof idea: place θ in the unit circle — the terminal point is (cos θ, sin θ); the radius is 1, so x² + y² = 1 gives the identity.…  ·  ## 3. Scientific Definitions | Term | Scientific meaning | Example | |---|---|---| | **Identity** | Equation holding for all admissible θ | sin²θ + cos²θ = 1 | | **Conditional identity** | a sinθ + b cosθ rewritten as a single sine with r, φ | 3sinθ + 4cosθ = 5sin(θ + 53.13°) | | **Transformation formula** | Converts sums of trig functions to products and back | sin C + sin D…

rows.label: More ideas
rows.text: tan(A + B) needs 1 - tan A tan B != 0; when it is zero the sum is 90° (mod 180°) and the tangent is undefined even though sin and cos are well defined.  ·  The identity sin(A + B) sin(A - B) = sin^2 A - sin^2 B is a product-to-sum result often asked as a proof, with the right side reached by expanding both factors.  ·  Because the standard values are exact surds, exact answers should be left as fractions with surds rather than rounded decimals.

rows.text: ## 4. Detailed Explanation ### 4.1 Why identities are "proved", not "solved" - A proof starts from one side and transforms it with known identities into the other; no values of θ are ever substituted. Solving an equation, by contrast, finds *which* θ make it true — the distinction is examinable.…  ·  ## 5. Comparison Tables **The three Pythagorean identities and their rearrangements** | Identity | Solved for sin² | Solved for cos² | |---|---|---| | sin²θ + cos²θ = 1 | sin²θ = 1 − cos²θ | cos²θ = 1 − sin²θ | | 1 + tan²θ = sec²θ | — | sec²θ − tan²θ = 1 | | 1 + cot²θ = cosec²θ | cosec²θ − cot²θ = 1 | — |  ·  ## 6. Common Confusions **cos(A − B) has a plus sign:** cos A cos B **+** sin A sin B — students carry the minus over from the argument.

rows.label: More ideas
rows.text: **tan(A ± B) denominators:** minus in the denominator for the **sum**, plus for the **difference** — the reverse of intuition.  ·  **Half-angle sign:** √((1−cosθ)/2) needs the quadrant of θ/2 — never quote the ± silently.  ·  ## 7.
